subject: Order form commercial finalization — checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@acme-cloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Order form — pricing schedule & tax clarifications

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile. Before we circulate the Order Form to our procurement/legal teams, I need a couple of clarifications so we can move to an internal purchase order: 

- Pricing schedule: can you confirm tiered pricing per token for 1–5M / 5–20M / 20M+ monthly usage and whether overage is billed monthly or pro-rated?
- Minimum commit: the draft references an "annual minimum commitment" — our CFO prefers shorter committed tranches. Is there a quarterly tranche option?
- Net terms & invoicing: we typically run Net 60. Is Redwood able to support Net 60 and quarterly invoicing, or is Net 45 the minimum? Also need to confirm what billing entity name and tax ID will appear on the invoice.
- Taxes: we need Redwood to confirm whether you will charge VAT (we are EU/US hybrid) and what evidence you need from us (VAT ID / W-9).

If you can provide a redline of the Order Form showing proposed invoicing schedule and a short checklist of items we need to return (PO, tax docs, billing contact), that would be great.

Attaching the draft we've been using on our side for reference (not the official PO).

Thanks,
Kerry
Procurement Lead, Acme Cloud

[attachment: ACME_Draft_OrderForm_stub.pdf (pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — pricing schedule & tax clarifications

Hi Kerry — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Markus (legal) and Karthik (finance) to make sure we provide a consolidated redline. Quick answers up-front: 

- Pricing: Redwood supports a tiered per-token model. I'll attach a summary table and include sample monthly invoices. Overage is billed on the next invoice (monthly).
- Minimum commit: we can offer an annual commitment OR a quarterly-committed plan where the annual dollar commitment is broken into four equal quarterly tranches. That is how we typically accommodate shorter procurement cycles.
- Net terms: our standard enterprise offering is Net 45, but we can accommodate Net 60 for first-time pilots with a quarterly invoicing cadence. After the first six months we can revisit and potentially convert to Net 30 with an early-pay credit. Karthik, please chime in if that requires finance approval.
- Taxes: Redwood will charge VAT where required and will list applicable taxes separately on the invoice. We'll need your VAT ID (EU) or W-9 (US) to support tax-exempt handling where appropriate.

Attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf (redline-ready). Markus will prepare legal comments and a redline focused on Order Form commercial clauses (pricing table, commit language, invoicing schedule, taxes).

Next steps: 
1) Markus to circulate legal redline by EOD 11/25.
2) Karthik to confirm final invoicing cadence and whether finance needs GL or PO templates.
3) Kerry to confirm billing entity name and provide tax docs.

Thanks — 
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> Hi Kerry — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Markus (legal) and Karthik (finance) to make sure we provide a consolidated redline.

Thanks Hannah — that reads well. A couple of follow-ups from procurement & legal on our side: 

- Quarterly tranche: acceptable in principle, but we need an explicit clause that unused quarterly committed dollars can be rolled forward once within the same contract year (we cannot forfeit value mid-year). Is that possible?
- VAT / tax evidence: Benjamin (CC'd) will send our EU VAT number and confirm whether we will be billed to Acme Global Ltd (EU) or Acme US Inc — please confirm which billing entity Redwood needs to invoice.
- Net 60: happy to accept Net 60 for the pilot as long as there is clear milestone invoicing (quarterly) and that payment due dates are tied to invoice date.

Benjamin: can you review Markus' forthcoming redline and flag anything at the tax/indemnity level?

I’ll aim to have our PO ready once we have the redline and a confirmed billing entity.

Best,
Kerry
Procurement Lead, Acme Cloud

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Benjamin Carter <benjamin.carter@acme-cloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T13:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — pricing schedule & tax clarifications — redline attached

Hannah / team / Benjamin — please find attached our proposed redline (OrderForm_redline_ACME_v3_markus.pdf). Key commercial/legal touchpoints summarized below: 

1) Commit & rollover: we can accept quarterly tranches with one-time rollover of unused quarterly committed dollars within the same 12-month term. Language added: "Customer may roll forward up to 1x of the unused quarterly committed amount to a subsequent quarter within the same contract year; unused amounts remaining at the end of the contract year shall expire."

2) Invoicing cadence & payment terms: redline proposes quarterly invoices issued in arrears with Net 60 for the initial six months; after six months either party may request conversion to Net 30 subject to Redwood credit approval. We added an early-payment credit option (1.5% if paid within 15 days) — optional and to be toggled in the Order Form.

3) Taxes: revised tax clause to read: "Customer shall be responsible for all sales, use, value added or similar transaction taxes imposed on amounts payable under this Order Form, excluding Redwood's income taxes. Customer shall provide applicable tax registration numbers (VAT ID, W-9, or equivalent) prior to the first invoice to enable correct tax treatment."

4) Billing entity: please confirm the exact legal entity name & tax ID to be used on invoices. We prefer a single billing entity per contract to avoid split invoices.

5) Overages & proration: clarified in Section 2 — overages will be billed on the next scheduled invoice; if a customer upgrades commitment mid-quarter we'll pro-rate the commit for that quarter.

Ben / Acme legal: two items for you to confirm from a tax/cross-border perspective — whether Acme wants Redwood to net VAT on the invoice or show VAT as separate line (we typically show separate VAT line), and whether Acme requires gross-up language for withholding taxes.

If that looks reasonable I can consolidate into a final OrderForm_consolidated_ACME_v4.pdf for signature.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
